case_context.protocol: Benzyl azide (0.50 mmol, 1.0 equiv) and phenylacetylene (0.55 mmol, 1.1 equiv) were combined with Cu/C catalyst (10 mol% Cu) in acetone (2.0 mL; benzyl azide concentration 0.25 M). The homogeneous liquid reaction mixture was heated under microwave batch conditions at 150 °C for 3 min. The corresponding 1,4-disubstituted 1,2,3-triazole was isolated in 94% yield.
case_context.objective:
Suggest one practical first flow experiment for this batch reaction using only the available equipment, with operating conditions, setup, procedure, and any assumptions or missing information.

Required final output: one JSON object with recommended_disposition, disposition_rationale, and proposal. The proposal must be a JSON object, not a JSON-encoded string. The proposal uses these fields:

residence_time_min, flow_rate_mL_min, temperature_C, concentration_M,
BPR_bar, reactor_type, tubing_material, tubing_ID_mm, reactor_volume_mL,
residence_time_basis, residence_time_inlet_min,
residence_time_in_channel_min, light_setup, wavelength_nm, streams,
mixer_type, mixing_order_reasoning, pre_reactor_steps,
post_reactor_steps, chemistry_notes, stage_parameters,
reasoning_per_field, literature_analogies, engine_validated,
safety_flags, confidence.

Each stream is an object with stream_label, pump_role, contents, solvent,
phase, flow_rate_mL_min, concentration_M, molar_equiv, gas_flow_sccm, and
gas_flow_actual_mL_min where applicable. Distinguish inlet/STP gas flow from
pressure-corrected in-channel gas flow. Ensure reactor_volume_mL is consistent
with flow and residence time. State assumptions rather than inventing missing
facts.

recommended_disposition must be exactly EXECUTE, SCREEN, or BLOCK. Use BLOCK
when the hard constraints make a safe design physically or operationally
impossible. Use SCREEN for a feasible first experiment that still requires
experimental validation. Use EXECUTE only for a directly executable design
supported by sufficient evidence.

operating_procedure.instruction: Prepare Stream A: on a 1.2 mL final-volume basis, charge benzyl azide: 0.3 mmol (0.25 M final); phenylacetylene: 0.33 mmol (0.275 M final); add acetone to 1.2 mL total. Convert mmol to weighed/dispensed amount using the verified reagent MW, assay, and density recorded at preparation. The 1.2 mL basis is only the minimum consumed at the final feed rate during 2.4 min of commissioning and initial collection. Before preparation, add measured feed-line displacement, pump/reservoir hold-up and any extra startup or collection allowance. For an added duration, add this stream's flow rate multiplied by the extra minutes. Scale every solute amount and final solvent volume by the same factor to retain concentrations and reagent ratios. Confirm sufficient reagent availability and container capacity; no dead-volume allowance or available stock has been assumed. Provide priming and shutdown solvent separately. This schedule assumes continuous feeding; a finite sample-loop injection requires a separately specified loading and collection schedule.

Allow an initial commissioning interval of at least 1.8 min, using three times the larger of the declared total reactor-time index and the sum of stage volume divided by local liquid flow. Confirm steady outlet composition and stable flow, pressure and temperature before collection; elapsed time alone does not establish steady state. Measure phase holdup or tracer response when gas or a packed bed is present. Budget additional feed for any extension before starting the run.

operating_procedure.instruction: After measured steady state, collect a timed fraction over at least 0.6 min as an initial sampling interval; record exact start/end times and collected mass or volume. Extend collection if needed for the analytical method, with feed stocks scaled to the revised duration.

Collect the crude outlet in the assigned vessel and retain a labeled aliquot for conversion, selectivity, and yield analysis. This first screen ends at crude collection; no isolation work-up is authorized unless the chemist adds a confirmed downstream procedure to the intake package.
Stop reactive feeds, flush each compatible line, cool the reactor to a safe handling temperature, and isolate energy sources.
Depressurize only through the controlled outlet while monitoring the pressure indicator; verify zero pressure before opening any fitting.

On leak, blockage, pressure excursion, or temperature excursion: stop reactive feeds and energy input, maintain only the hazard-appropriate purge/cooling path, isolate sources, and follow the laboratory emergency plan.
Collect product, flush, quench, and vent-associated waste in separately labeled containers compatible with the declared hazards; do not combine incompatible waste streams.

chemistry_notes.text: CuAAC [3+2] cycloaddition of benzyl azide with phenylacetylene over heterogeneous Cu/C packed bed. Mechanism: Cu(I) surface sites (generated in situ from Cu(0)/Cu(I) equilibrium on carbon support) activate phenylacetylene to form copper(I) acetylide, which coordinates benzyl azide to form a dinuclear Cu-azide-acetylide pi-complex (rate-limiting step), followed by ring closure to Cu(III) triazolide metallacycle and protodemetalation to release 1-benzyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3-triazole with exclusive 1,4-regioselectivity. Key design decisions: (1) BPR at 20 bar is mandatory — acetone bp 56 °C, operating at 150 °C requires >11.8 bar to maintain liquid phase; 20 bar is the only available setpoint and is appropriate. (2) Single-stream design: no incompatible pairs require stream separation; benzyl azide and phenylacetylene do not react at RT without Cu catalyst. (3) Cu/C is contained in CatCart — eliminates catalyst filtration, provides high surface-area-to-volume ratio for mass transfer. (4) Benzyl azide is a primary organic azide — shock/heat sensitive in bulk; flow confinement in 0.3 mL reactor volume dramatically reduces explosive risk vs. batch; blast shield mandatory. (5) Engineering calculations flag Da >> 1 (mass-transfer limited) and Pe = 4 (significant axial dispersion in 4 mm ID cartridge); the packed bed geometry partially mitigates both by providing tortuous flow paths and high catalyst surface area. (6) Analogy 1 (azide chemistry, copper reactor, PFA tubing, 120 °C, 30 min, 0.45 M, 8 bar BPR) is chemically closest but uses a homogeneous copper-coil reactor at lower temperature with much longer residence time — not directly applicable for hardware parameters. Our packed-bed CatCart at 150 °C with heterogeneous Cu/C is expected to be significantly faster. (7) Residence time of 0.6 min is slightly above the calculated range of 0.2-0.5 min but is dictated by the fixed 0.3 mL CatCart volume at 0.5 mL/min — experimentally screen flow rates 0.3-1.0 mL/min to optimize. Recommended disposition: SCREEN.

residence_time_min.authority: non-executable original model rationale; arithmetic superseded by final calculation audit

source_record.text: Calculation estimated 0.3 min (range 0.2-0.5 min) based on 10x intensification factor from batch 3 min. Fixed inventory reactor is 0.3 mL CatCart; at 0.5 mL/min (minimum practical flow for X-Cube HPLC pump with good control), residence time = 0.3/0.5 = 0.6 min. This is slightly above the calculated upper bound but is dictated by hardware constraints. Analogy 1 (similar azide chemistry, copper reactor): chemically similar in using copper catalyst and azide substrate, key difference is homogeneous copper-coil at 120 °C with 30 min residence time vs. our heterogeneous packed bed at 150 °C — heterogeneous packed bed at higher temperature is expected to be much faster, so 30 min from Analogy 1 is not applicable; we use the calculation-derived estimate adjusted to hardware. Analogy 2 ([3+2] cycloaddition, CFU, 60 °C, 20 min): chemically similar mechanism class but much lower temperature and no Cu catalyst — 20 min not applicable at 150 °C with Cu/C. Analogy 3 (heterogeneous catalyst packed bed, 0.04 mL/min, 3 mL reactor): similar heterogeneous catalyst concept but different chemistry and very slow flow — not applicable. Screening flow rates 0.3-1.0 mL/min (residence times 0.3-1.0 min) is recommended.

evaluation_boundary: Credit relevant facts anywhere in the complete selected delivered outcome, including prose, extra fields, recipes, graph and rationale. Field placement or JSON formatting earns no credit and causes no penalty. Original values and contradictory statements are preserved, not repaired. Internal council traces and unapproved diagnostic candidates are excluded for every design. Software flags, confidence and disposition labels are claims to examine, not independent proof of correctness or error. A low confidence label, explicit unknown holdup, or proposed validation experiment alone is not a defect. A withheld executable artifact remains a delivery limitation. Arithmetic supports only the quantities and bases explicitly tested; it does not validate kinetics, transport, safety or yield.
